Chiral PTCs are important type of organocatalysts and have

chiral PTC combined catalysis has emerged as a highly
promising strategy in asymmetric catalysis.<sup>15</sup>

We initiated a systematic study of the Pd/chiral PTC-
catalyzed asymmetric allenylic alkylation using racemic
allenylic acetate 1a and oxindole 2a as model substrates
(Table 1). Several commercially available ligands (L1−L4)
were evaluated in the presence of an L-isoleucine-derived
quaternary phosphonium salt (PTC-1). While these systems
could deliver the desired allylic allenylation product 3aa, both
the enantioselectivity and diastereoselectivity proved unsat-
isfactory (entries 1−4). The observed suboptimal stereo-
control may be attributed to competing background reactivity
mediated by a single Pd/ligand catalytic cycle. Inspired by
findings from Takemoto<sup>14b</sup> and Zi,<sup>15f</sup> the deliberate use of
electronically more deficeint phosphite ligand L5 would be
able to slow down the competing monocatalytic process.
Remarkably, this approach not only substantially enhanced
enantioselectivity but also significantly improved diastereose-
lectivity, albeit at the expense of the reaction yield (entry 5).
Subsequently, screening of various phase-transfer catalysts
(PTCs) identified PTC-3 as the optimal, demonstrating
remarkable enhancement in the yield, diastereoselectivity,
and enantioselectivity. These results strongly suggest a
synergistic catalytic efect between ligands L5 and PTC-3, as
evidenced by comparative evaluation of diferent PTC systems
(entry 7). Base optimization (entries 11−15) identified NaOH
as critical for maximizing both reactivity and selectivity in the
L5/PTC-3 system, achieving peak performance (entry 14).
